title: Corollary 'Why grids are nearly optimal': torus/Fourier optimality and 'boundary corrections' asserted without proof

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Corollary following Theorem `\label{thm:anticipated}` ('Why grids are nearly optimal for $R$').

The corollary states 'for a translation-invariant $C$ on a torus the grid is the exact minimizer of (UKvar) by Fourier diagonalization, and on a bounded $D$ it is optimal up to boundary corrections.' Neither claim is proved: the Fourier-diagonalization optimality on the torus is asserted in one clause, and 'optimal up to boundary corrections' is not quantified. The supporting 'space-filling' language and the duplicate-point argument are heuristic and do not establish that the regular grid minimizes $\Var(R)-\mathbf c^\top\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf c$ among all $n$-point configurations.

**Suggested fix.** Either prove the torus statement explicitly (diagonalize the circulant covariance over a regular grid via the DFT and show the variance criterion is minimized by the uniform grid among $n$-point configurations on the torus), or relabel the corollary as a heuristic remark and remove the optimality claim.
